name: Sun
atmosphere: Photosphere ~5772 K effective; chromosphere and corona (~1-2 million K) above; composition ~73% H, 25% He by mass.
notes: G2V star. Rotation: Carrington synodic-sidereal ~25.38 d at 26 deg latitude; faster at equator (~24.5 d), slower at poles (~34 d). Axial tilt is relative to the ecliptic. Luminosity 3.828e26 W.

name: Mercury
atmosphere: Exosphere only (traces of O, Na, H, He, K); surface pressure ~1e-14 bar.
notes: 3:2 spin-orbit resonance; one solar day = ~176 Earth days. Radius is mean radius. Inclination to the ecliptic.

name: Venus
atmosphere: 96.5% CO2, 3.5% N2; surface pressure ~92 bar, surface ~737 K; sulfuric-acid cloud decks.
notes: Retrograde rotation (243 d). Surface texture is a radar-derived/artistic map; atmosphere texture in venus_atmosphere.jpg.

name: Earth
atmosphere: 78% N2, 21% O2, 0.9% Ar, ~0.04% CO2, variable H2O; surface pressure 1.013 bar.
notes: Mean radius. Sidereal rotation 23h 56m 4s. Orbit is the ecliptic by definition (semimajor axis of Earth-Moon barycenter).

name: Mars
atmosphere: ~95% CO2, 2.8% N2, 2% Ar; surface pressure ~0.006 bar.
notes: Mean radius (equatorial 3396.2 km, polar 3376.2 km).

name: Jupiter

ring.note: Faint main ring plus halo/gossamer rings out to ~226000 km; no texture supplied.

atmosphere: ~90% H2, ~10% He by number; ammonia, water and ammonium hydrosulfide clouds; Great Red Spot.
notes: Radius is the 1-bar mean radius (equatorial 71492 km). Rotation is System III.

name: Saturn

ring.note: Spans the C, B and A rings (D ring starts ~66900 km, F ring ~140200 km). Gaps: Cassini Division, Encke Gap.

atmosphere: ~96% H2, ~3% He; ammonia ice clouds; polar hexagon.
notes: Radius is the 1-bar mean radius (equatorial 60268 km). Mean density 687 kg/m3, less than water.

name: Uranus

ring.note: 13 known narrow rings from the 6 ring to the epsilon ring plus dusty inner rings; no texture supplied.

atmosphere: ~83% H2, ~15% He, ~2% CH4 (gives the cyan colour).
notes: Rotates on its side; retrograde. Radius is the 1-bar mean radius (equatorial 25559 km).

name: Neptune

ring.note: Galle, Le Verrier, Lassell/Arago and Adams rings (with arcs); faint, dusty; no texture supplied.

atmosphere: ~80% H2, ~19% He, ~1.5% CH4; fastest winds in the Solar System (~2000 km/h).
notes: Radius is the 1-bar mean radius (equatorial 24764 km).

name: Pluto
atmosphere: Thin N2 atmosphere with CH4 and CO; surface pressure ~1 Pa (~10 microbar) and varies seasonally.
notes: Dwarf planet. Orbit semi-major axis, eccentricity and inclination vary noticeably over time (osculating, approximate). Pluto-Charon barycentre lies outside Pluto. Albedo is approx (Bond estimates range ~0.4-0.7).

name: Moon
notes: Inclination is to the ecliptic; axial tilt 1.54 deg to the ecliptic (6.68 deg to its orbit). Semimajor axis changes ~3.8 cm/yr. Rotation is synchronous with the orbit (tilt assumed ~0 relative to the orbital plane).

name: Phobos
notes: Mean radius; irregular (27 x 22 x 18 km). Orbits below synchronous altitude and spirals inward. Rotation is synchronous with the orbit (tilt assumed ~0 relative to the orbital plane).

name: Deimos
notes: Mean radius; irregular (15 x 12 x 10 km). Rotation is synchronous with the orbit (tilt assumed ~0 relative to the orbital plane).

name: Io
notes: Most volcanically active body known; tidally heated. Rotation is synchronous with the orbit (tilt assumed ~0 relative to the orbital plane).

name: Europa
notes: Ice shell over a global subsurface ocean. Rotation is synchronous with the orbit (tilt assumed ~0 relative to the orbital plane).

name: Ganymede
notes: Largest moon in the Solar System; has an intrinsic magnetic field. Rotation is synchronous with the orbit (tilt assumed ~0 relative to the orbital plane).

name: Callisto
notes: Heavily cratered; possibly partially differentiated. Rotation is synchronous with the orbit (tilt assumed ~0 relative to the orbital plane).

name: Titan
notes: Only moon with a dense atmosphere; liquid methane/ethane lakes. Albedo approximate (opaque haze). Rotation is synchronous with the orbit (tilt assumed ~0 relative to the orbital plane).

name: Enceladus
atmosphere: Thin water-vapour plume over the south pole.
notes: Geysers feed Saturn's E ring; subsurface ocean. Rotation is synchronous with the orbit (tilt assumed ~0 relative to the orbital plane).

name: Mimas
notes: Large Herschel crater. Rotation is synchronous with the orbit (tilt assumed ~0 relative to the orbital plane).

name: Rhea
notes: Second largest moon of Saturn. Rotation is synchronous with the orbit (tilt assumed ~0 relative to the orbital plane).

name: Iapetus
notes: Two-tone surface: leading hemisphere very dark (albedo ~0.03-0.05), trailing hemisphere bright (~0.5-0.6); equatorial ridge. Inclination is to the Laplace plane. Rotation is synchronous with the orbit (tilt assumed ~0 relative to the orbital plane).

name: Miranda
notes: Mean radius; patchwork terrain, Verona Rupes cliff. Mass approximate. Rotation is synchronous with the orbit (tilt assumed ~0 relative to the orbital plane).

name: Titania
notes: Largest moon of Uranus. Rotation is synchronous with the orbit (tilt assumed ~0 relative to the orbital plane).

name: Oberon
notes: Outermost major moon of Uranus. Rotation is synchronous with the orbit (tilt assumed ~0 relative to the orbital plane).

name: Triton
notes: Retrograde orbit (likely captured Kuiper-belt object); nitrogen geysers. Inclination >90 deg = retrograde. Rotation is synchronous with the orbit (tilt assumed ~0 relative to the orbital plane).

name: Charon
notes: Pluto and Charon are mutually tidally locked (double synchronous). Axial tilt relative to its orbit ~0. Rotation is synchronous with the orbit (tilt assumed ~0 relative to the orbital plane).
